dd8dbc78-e5ae-46ce-963c-81e815eeb1e3: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

b39e659f-b678-48b6-a9bd-a80a7704e249: with Pedrito Martínez Following his spectacular performance last season as part of Terence Blanchard’s UpSwing series, Cuban piano savant Alfredo Rodríguez returns with his powerful Afro-Cuban ensemble featuring the dynamic percussion master Pedrito Martínez for this evening of rhythmic fireworks. After Quincy Jones first heard Alfredo Rodríguez at the Monteux Jazz Festival in 2006 the legendary producer guided his ascent as Rodríguez became one of Cuba’s most visible and creatively unfettered musicians. Based in Los Angeles since he defected in 2009, the pianist has released a series of increasingly expansive albums for Mack Avenue, incorporating sounds from South India, Argentina, Spain, the Middle East and beyond. His formidable technique and soulful approach was described by the Mercury News as “the way Monk might have sounded if he had been born in Chick Corea’s body and raised on a diet of Bach, Chopin and Stravinsky in a Havana conservatory.” Released on his own Take Cover imprint, Rodriguez’s new album is a blistering collection of standards and covers called ¡Take Cover! that includes his takes on the music of Tito Puente, Henry Mancini, Stevie Wonder, The Eagles, Lalo Shifrin, and more. Personnel: Alfredo Rodríguez (piano); Pedrito Martínez (percussion); Others TBA

5018ed97-4825-4e1f-8166-dcdb1be4c748: The final season installment of Terence Blanchard’s wildly popular UpSwing concert series highlights a pair of instrumentalists forging singular careers guided by uncompromising artistic vision. Los Angeles-based keyboardist and producer Julian Pollack, known widely as J3PO, is among the most exciting young artists on the scene. Raised in Berkeley, he was an award-winning member of the SFJAZZ High School All-Stars and appeared on Marian McPartland’s iconic Piano Jazz program on NPR at age 18. Since then, Pollack has emerged as a visionary force bridging jazz virtuosity with electronic production, hip-hop, and experimental sound design. He has worked with artists across jazz and contemporary music while developing a distinctive solo voice that positions him at the forefront of a new generation redefining jazz for the digital age. Vibraphonist Joel Ross has earned widespread renown as the most remarkable young voice on his instrument. Since the 2019 release of Ross’ debut album Kingmaker on Blue Note, he’s quickly established himself as a triple threat with a far-reaching approach. A graduate of Stockton’s University of the Pacific, Ross went on to study jazz at The New School and was mentored by former SFJAZZ Collective vibraphonist Stefon Harris. His new Blue Note release, Gospel Music, is a sonic interpretation of the Biblical story and an exploration of faith, featuring an expanded sextet lineup of his Good Vibes band. d46420ce-f981-45a3-beff-cb0f989639bf: Timeless Brazilian grooves with fresh arrangements and uplifting energy · The iconic sound of Sergio Mendes returns to the stage as Gracinha Leporace leads The Sergio Mendes Band in a spirited celebration of his life, joy, and musical legacy. Marking sixty years since the worldwide debut of Brasil ’66, this revitalized ensemble continues Mendes’ lifelong mission of sharing the vibrant rhythms and infectious soul of Brazilian music with audiences around the world. “Carrying Sergio’s music forward is both an honor and a responsibility,” said Gracinha Leporace. “This band embodies his spirit, joy, and deep love for Brazilian music. Sergio cherished every single member of this extraordinary ensemble, and we’re proud to continue what he started.” With a sound that blends timeless Brazilian grooves with fresh arrangements and uplifting energy, The Sergio Mendes Band brings a renewed sense of celebration to every performance. Each note pays tribute to Mendes’ remarkable inﬂuence — a career that helped shape the global appreciation of Bossa Nova, Samba, and the unmistakable warmth of Brazilian culture. About The Sergio Mendes Band The ensemble features: · Gracinha Leporace and Katie Hampton – Vocals · Leo Costa – Drums · Gibi dos Santos – Percussion · Kleber Jorge – Guitar & Vocals · Andre de Santanna – Bass · Scott Mayo – Keys, Saxophone, Flute & Vocals · Jamieson Trotter – Piano Together, the artists uphold Mendes’ vision of spreading joy through music — performing with the same passion, precision, and energy that captivated global audiences for over six decades. Continuing Legacy The Sergio Mendes Band invites long-term fans and new listeners alike to experience the sounds that deﬁned generations. Through their upcoming shows, they honor Sergio’s enduring message: that music has the power to unite, uplift, and bring people together from every part of the world.

3811ae0d-3267-49c0-b175-192a97ec0c55: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

c7a51d7e-05fe-441d-b383-3b48f829219b: Winner of the 2019 American Pianists Award and finalist in the 2011 Thelonious Monk International Piano Competition, virtuoso Emmet Cohen is among the most acclaimed pianists in jazz, known widely as a member of bass great Christian McBride’s Tip City and music director with vocal phenom Veronica Swift, along with his stellar work as a bandleader. He steps back on the Miner stage with his working quintet after his sold-out 2026 performance focused on the music of Miles Davis and John Coltrane in honor of their centennials. The prodigious pianist started piano studies at three and released his 2011 debut In the Element while still enrolled at University of Florida’s Frost School of Music. He has accumulated nearly 20 major awards and honors over his career and created the acclaimed Masters Legacy Series of recordings and interviews in 2016 featuring collaboration with Ron Carter, Benny Golson, Albert “Tootie” Heath, George Coleman, and Houston Person. Cohen has been a member of the bands led by drumming luminaries Herlin Riley and Ali Jackson and hosted the wildly popular YouTube series Live From Emmet’s Place with a procession of special guests. Cohen has led 12 albums including his newest Mack Avenue release, 2024’s Vibe Provider. Personnel: Emmet Cohen (piano); Others TBA
67ea8ba4-d58d-410c-aa8d-dfe177b534e8: Timeless Brazilian grooves with fresh arrangements and uplifting energy · The iconic sound of Sergio Mendes returns to the stage as Gracinha Leporace leads The Sergio Mendes Band in a spirited celebration of his life, joy, and musical legacy. Marking sixty years since the worldwide debut of Brasil ’66, this revitalized ensemble continues Mendes’ lifelong mission of sharing the vibrant rhythms and infectious soul of Brazilian music with audiences around the world. “Carrying Sergio’s music forward is both an honor and a responsibility,” said Gracinha Leporace. “This band embodies his spirit, joy, and deep love for Brazilian music. Sergio cherished every single member of this extraordinary ensemble, and we’re proud to continue what he started.” With a sound that blends timeless Brazilian grooves with fresh arrangements and uplifting energy, The Sergio Mendes Band brings a renewed sense of celebration to every performance. Each note pays tribute to Mendes’ remarkable inﬂuence — a career that helped shape the global appreciation of Bossa Nova, Samba, and the unmistakable warmth of Brazilian culture. About The Sergio Mendes Band The ensemble features: · Gracinha Leporace and Katie Hampton – Vocals · Leo Costa – Drums · Gibi dos Santos – Percussion · Kleber Jorge – Guitar & Vocals · Andre de Santanna – Bass · Scott Mayo – Keys, Saxophone, Flute & Vocals · Jamieson Trotter – Piano Together, the artists uphold Mendes’ vision of spreading joy through music — performing with the same passion, precision, and energy that captivated global audiences for over six decades. Continuing Legacy The Sergio Mendes Band invites long-term fans and new listeners alike to experience the sounds that deﬁned generations. Through their upcoming shows, they honor Sergio’s enduring message: that music has the power to unite, uplift, and bring people together from every part of the world.

d6bdf68a-79d2-4f7f-bef0-af2fbbb20490: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

1ebf6217-3408-41b5-a363-4750ea75e4c1: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

029d50a3-5858-46fb-a6e9-c730345d92a8: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

2454eee3-076d-4d9d-b8cb-4879d65f3a42: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

cfa4be27-ea14-4316-9870-75b6bc6cb7cb: A pair of master musicians representing the diversity of string instrument traditions, Derek Gripper and Alam Khan unite for a project that dissolves musical borders and reimagines the possibilities of global acoustic music. Gripper has earned international acclaim for his groundbreaking adaptations of West African kora music for solo guitar, a feat that led legendary kora master Toumani Diabaté to remark that Gripper had “taken the guitar to a new place.” His work bridges African classical traditions with jazz and contemporary composition, establishing him as one of the world’s most innovative guitarists. Alam Khan, the son of the legendary sarod maestro Ali Akbar Khan, carries forward one of India’s most revered musical lineages. A master of the sarod and a gifted composer, Khan blends the rigor of Hindustani classical music with adventurous cross-cultural collaboration, earning respect across both traditional and contemporary music circles. Together, Gripper and Khan engage in a transcendent musical conversation—an immersive journey through African, Indian, and contemporary sound worlds shaped by improvisation, technical brilliance, and deep cultural exchange. Personnel: Derek Gripper (guitar); Alam Khan (sarod)

56addc99-ce04-4346-b1ef-a0f718922435: Few artists embody the pulse of Latin jazz like Poncho Sánchez, a conguero whose hands seem to translate history into rhythm. He makes his first appearance at the SFJAZZ Center with this performance, joined by the latest iteration of his Latin Band. Born in Texas and raised in Southern California, Sánchez emerged from a rich blend of Afro-Cuban traditions and bebop influences, eventually becoming one of the most influential percussionists in jazz. His early mentorship under vibraphonist Cal Tjader positioned him at the heart of a lineage that includes giants like Tito Puente and Mongo Santamaría—artists who helped define the genre he now carries forward. With his band, Sánchez forged a sound that is both scholarly and electrifying: tight horn lines, driving congas, and an irresistible groove that merges jazz sophistication with street-level soul. Over decades and more than 20 albums, he has transformed Latin jazz into a living, evolving conversation, earning a GRAMMY and global acclaim. His latest project, Poncho Sánchez & His Latin Jazz Band Live at the Belly Up Tavern, captures that vitality in real time. The album delivers fresh arrangements and the kinetic energy of a live performance, proving that Sánchez’s music is not archival—it is alive, urgent, and still expanding. In every strike of the drum, Poncho Sánchez doesn’t just play Latin jazz—he sustains its heartbeat. Personnel: Poncho Sánchez (congas); Others TBA

69d289b3-c3da-48e8-8f07-03ff9e3f07df: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

b9f0e5df-480f-489f-8212-0ba45d3975e6: The most influential figure in modern Afro-Cuban jazz for more than half a century, virtuoso pianist, composer and arranger Chucho Valdés celebrates his 85th Birthday with this week of special concerts. The son of Cuban pianist Bebo Valdés, the winner of seven GRAMMYs and seven Latin GRAMMY Awards joined Armando Romeu’s celebrated Cuban Orchestra of Modern Music in 1967, a time when the communist government still considered American jazz anti-revolutionary. He was already recognized as the most formidable pianist of his generation when he launched Irakere in 1973 with a phenomenal cast that included saxophonist Paquito D’Rivera and trumpeter Arturo Sandoval. Over the ensuing years, Valdés has concentrated on his career as a solo artist, recording over 25 albums and co-writing the landmark 2018 book Decoding Afro-Cuban Jazz in collaboration with SFJAZZ Director of Education Rebeca Mauleón. His staggering legacy was summed up by the Boston Globe, who lauded him for “an encyclopedic vocabulary of Afro-Cuban rhythms and an expansive palette that includes all manner of modern jazz as well as traditional classical repertoire.” Most recently, Valdés has brought his Afro-Cuban Messengers, Irakere 50, and Royal Quartet projects to SFJAZZ, and for this 85th birthday celebration event, Valdés will be joined by a superlative lineup of musicians and special guests, ending the 2026-27 Season in grand fashion. Personnel: Chucho Valdés (piano); Others TBA

136866a4-8add-4b29-88b1-a51c62cf59db: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. 904b4ddb-1856-4c3f-bf90-b2d22d51b35a: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

6bdddeb2-1aad-4815-883f-cf52e2c72afc: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

00e0932d-7881-4d5c-8586-8183feb02ab4: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

2c3db5b4-b66a-4e97-97d2-e28134fa0c63: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

216d572c-1ff0-4cd1-8e4c-795e0e2b63b6: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

a720636b-2e44-4420-b64e-876282bdb552: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

7b3c8c8d-9a20-42a2-afa1-dbe962898ad7: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

9047a6e9-a473-4d55-ac30-1037b5a2b2cd: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

714aa0b8-96e8-41fc-acc9-937dac308823: The Magic’s Blue Cube initiative is where the promise of the Magic Theatre’s inception is taking root anew: this is the home for the weird, the slippage of time, the leap into pelagic zones of the theatrical imagination. Each year, The Blue Cube Initiative will host 2 productions in rep on the same set: one dedicated boundary-obliterating work from local writers, the other to non-traditional performances from the far-flung corners of the mainstream. In 2027, the Blue Cube Initiative kicks off with the world premiere of “5 Forgeries,” from Bay Area native Lucas Baisch: A grieving mother denies Munchausen by proxy. A teen prodigy lusts after a boy at school. A hospice nurse is convinced she’s possessed by a Central American dictator. A terminally ill artist scams their mentor. The performers craft model dioramas in real time, oscillating between monologue and scene, with each path leading to The Annual Convention – a cheap, carpeted hotel conference room. Through live-feed projection and scenic re-construction, this experimental play studies the inefficacy of control, the dispossession of land, the creeping rot of the body, and the twin definitions of “possession” as both a system of proprietary capture and a haunting.

7690a670-7b8d-41f9-8a1b-26c379f8b3ad: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

6cb57a35-f66e-4cd5-8064-879c3a3fe4d8: On the Third Thursday of every month, PULSE gathers at the Barn (unless otherwise announced on facebook) for our monthly fusion lesson and social! 7-8pm Class 8pm Opening Circle 8:15-10/10:30 (depending on season) Social Dance We have had a thriving dance community since 2022, which branches from the scene that was here before the pandemic (formerly known as North Bay Fusion). What is PULSE Partner Dance Collective? We invite you to cultivate your skills in communication, consent, nonverbal cues, and partnered dance movement and will be offering support via lessons before events - our own, and before other dances in the Sonoma County, CA region. 4c9589e4-c08b-4301-aac0-15bfb16ec21e: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

fc0c1918-1946-4a1b-8b64-ee28516cd64d: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.
